stemMd: A point on the unit circle has coordinates (−3/5, 4/5). If its angle from the positive horizontal axis is θ, what is sin θ?
explanationMd: On the unit circle the coordinates are (cos θ, sin θ). The vertical coordinate is therefore the sine, 4/5. Its positive sign agrees with the point being in the upper half-plane.

distractorRationale.d: This is the cosine, the horizontal coordinate.
distractorRationale.e: This changes the cosine’s sign but still uses the wrong coordinate.
distractorRationale.b: The point lies above the horizontal axis, so sine is positive.
distractorRationale.a: This is the tangent, the ratio of vertical to horizontal coordinates.
